_description: Single SoT for the Surface Pro 8 bootloader: UEFI/NVRAM, GRUB install + UI + menu, kernel cmdline (hibernate slice), initrd, LUKS, swap. Phase 1 captures current behavior; Phase 3 yields full grub.cfg authority from NixOS to this SoT.

engine._description: Engine policy — replaces the scattered env-var flags (YES, DRY_RUN, NO_NVRAM, DEFAULT_BOOT, SKIP_KERNELS, SKIP_GRUB_BIN, REBUILD_ACTION, FLAKE_MODULES_DIR) that previously controlled per-install-script behaviour. Each install-*.sh reads its slice from here. Env vars STILL override (for ad-hoc surgical runs and CI), but JSON is canonical. Setting interactive=false makes the engine declarative-by-default — no Proceed?[y/N] prompt, the JSON IS the decision.

grub_install._description: Knobs for engine/install-grub.sh. include_kernels=false skips /boot/kernels copy (faster re-deploy if kernels are unchanged); include_binaries=false skips grubx64.efi + modules (when only grub.cfg changed).

nixos_install._description: Knobs for engine/install-nixos.sh. trigger_rebuild = none|boot|switch|test|dry-build (if not 'none', engine runs nixos-rebuild after dropping modules into the host flake — but the recommended pattern is to leave this 'none' and let the host flake's build.sh switch own that step). flake_modules_dir is the destination for adapter modules; relative paths resolve against aa_bootloader/ root.
nixos_install._flake_modules_dir_note: Host flake was renamed from aa_nixos-surface_host → aa_desk-usr_x86_surface-linux_nixos as part of the unix/ directory taxonomy refactor. Engine resolves relative paths against ROOT_DIR (= aa_bootloader/).

nvram._description: aa_bootloader owns NVRAM. deploy-grub.sh runs nvram/apply.sh which idempotently ensures these entries exist via efibootmgr.
nvram._ownership_note: GRUB EFI binary lives at /EFI/bootloader/grubx64.efi — neutral install dir, no distro owns it (2026-05-07 migration from /EFI/NixOS-boot-efi/). UEFI firmware doesn't care about dirname semantics; this name reflects that aa_bootloader is the SoT and the binary is overwritten on every `build.sh deploy-grub`. No distro's apt/pacman/grub-install can collide with this path.
nvram._remove_stale_note: On deploy-nvram, efibootmgr removes any NVRAM entries with these labels. NixOS-boot-efi is the legacy name we used before 2026-05-07 — this purges the stale boot variable so firmware doesn't hold a dangling reference after the install dir was renamed.

refind._description: rEFInd boot manager — primary bootloader as of Phase 4. Lives on ESP at /boot/efi/EFI/refind/. Auto-detects most OSes via EFI binary discovery; manual_stanzas overrides anything that needs hand-curated cmdlines/initrds.

install._drivers_note: iso9660_x64 dropped — not used by any menu entry. ntfs/hfs unneeded.
install._tools_dir_note: Sub-directory under /EFI/refind/ where vendored EFI binaries (shellx64.efi, memtest86.efi, ipxe.efi) live. Emitted as 'tools_dir tools' in refind.conf so rEFInd's bottom-row tool buttons (showtools) can find their binaries — without this, shellx64.efi at /EFI/refind/tools/ falls outside rEFInd's default search paths (/EFI/refind/, /EFI/tools/, /EFI/) and the 'shell' button silently no-ops.

theme._description: rEFInd theme. Vendored at src/loaders/refind/vendored/themes/<name>/. The renderer (a) copies that dir to dist/.../refind/themes/<name>/ and (b) uses the theme_conf shipped by upstream (or generates one) — so paths/sizes/variant are always data-driven from this block.
theme.name: catppuccin
theme._layout_note: Catppuccin/mocha variant. Per-variant layout: assets/<variant>/{background.png,selection_big.png,selection_small.png,icons/}. Catppuccin upstream's tool/func icon set is sparse (no tool_rescue/tool_fwupdate/tool_memtest/tool_netboot/func_install/func_bootorder/os_refind), so we backfilled those 7 PNGs into assets/mocha/icons/ from brads-refind-theme to keep the second-line tool row complete. All first-line OS icons (os_nixos/os_kali/os_debian/os_linux/vol_external/...) come from upstream catppuccin → consistent style. Switched 2026-05-07 from brads-refind-theme (which had Catppuccin-backfilled OS icons mixed with Brad's tool icons → visually inconsistent first row).
theme._icon_size_note: POST-2026-05-16: bumped from 128/48 to 256/96 to match Catppuccin's native icon sizes. Observed bug: with big_icon_size=128, the first-row OS icons (256→128 downscale path) silently failed to render — rEFInd fell back to its default generic icons. Tool row (96→48 downscale) rendered correctly, so the bug is specific to the 50% downscale of the larger RGBA OS icons on this firmware. Setting native sizes (no scaling) bypasses the bug. On Surface Pro 8 2880×1920 display, 256-px OS icons = ~13% of vertical = fine. Old comment: 128/48 was an aesthetic preference, never tested whether scaling actually worked.
theme._banner_note: Catppuccin/mocha background (dark base02 backdrop). banner_scale=fillscreen lets it scale to the Surface's 2880x1920 panel.
theme._font_note: Empty = use rEFInd's bundled default ASCII font (Luxi Mono Regular 12pt). Catppuccin ships no font atlas. ASCII labels in manual_stanzas.order ensure no '??' glyphs.
theme._show_label_note: rEFInd's graphical UI shows the label of the currently-selected icon only — engine-level constraint, not a theme setting. show_label=true keeps that label visible; false adds 'label' to hideui.
theme._variant_note: Catppuccin variants: latte (light), frappe (mid-dark), macchiato (dark), mocha (darkest). Mocha matches the SP8 default Plasma dark theme. Switching variant requires updating: variant + theme_conf + icons_path + banner_path + selection_*_path together.

testers._description: Post-deploy invariants for the active theme. Run after `aa_bootloader/build.sh deploy-refind` to confirm rEFInd will actually load what boot.json says.

checks.description: Theme dir exists on EFI partition
Generated theme.conf has the filename declared in theme.theme_conf — without this the include line points at upstream's bundled mocha.conf (wrong paths) and our paths are silently ignored
Every per-entry first-line icon referenced in refind.manual_stanzas.order resolves to a real file on /boot/efi
checks.command: for i in os_nixos os_kali os_debian os_android os_linux vol_external os_refind tool_rescue tool_fwupdate tool_memtest tool_netboot tool_shell func_install func_bootorder; do test -f /boot/efi/EFI/refind/themes/catppuccin/assets/mocha/icons/$i.png || { echo MISSING:$i; exit 1; }; done; echo ok

checks.description: Deployed background.png is byte-identical to vendored source — proves the engine actually copied the new theme's banner
refind.conf include line points at the same theme_conf the generator writes

ui._showtools_note: Bottom-row tool icons. rEFInd renders each one IFF it's either built-in (no external binary) or its EFI binary is on the ESP and inside rEFInd's tool search path (defaults + tools_dir). Add a tool here only after vendoring its EFI binary into src/loaders/refind/vendored/efi-tools/ AND declaring it in refind.tools.
ui._enable_touch_note: Surface Pro 8 has a digitiser/touchscreen exposed by UEFI. Tapping a top-row icon selects+activates it. Off by default in rEFInd; enabled here for Surface ergonomics.
ui._enable_mouse_note: USB/BT mouse pointer. Off by default — touchscreen via enable_touch is the primary input on this device. Toggle to true if a peripheral mouse is attached at boot.

scan._description: Mode B: manual-only. The menu is exactly what aa_bootloader generates from boot.json. No autodetect surprises.

refind._tools_note: Vendored EFI utilities staged on the ESP at /EFI/refind/<tools_dir>/. Each entry: { source: filename in src/loaders/refind/vendored/efi-tools/, dest: filename written to the ESP, used_by: array of showtools keywords or menu entries that need this binary }. render-refind-binary.sh stages these; rEFInd's bottom-row showtools auto-finds them once tools_dir is set; manual_stanzas.order entries reference them via efi_chainload.

tools._upstream: memtest.org — nixpkgs.memtest86plus 7.00 (Linux EFI-stub bzImage; rEFInd loads via the PE32+ headers within)
ipxe.org — nixpkgs.ipxe (network boot — chain into PXE/HTTP/TFTP)

manual_stanzas._description: Ordered top-level entries shown in rEFInd. Each item picks a 'producer' (built-in renderer) and overrides the display label. NixOS data comes from /nix/var/nix/profiles; OS data comes from grub.menu.* via the 'from' field.
manual_stanzas._integration_note: integration declares per-OS coupling — adapter = files dropped INTO the OS so it yields bootloader control to us (NixOS gets nixos_yield.nix + kernel staging); passive = we read the OS's kernels at their existing path, OS unaware (Kali, Debian: apt manages /vmlinuz, we just point at it); chainload = we hand control to the OS's own EFI binary with no integration (Windows, Ventoy, refind_self).
manual_stanzas._icon_note: Per-stanza 'icon' field overrides the producer default. Use bare basename (no .png extension); the renderer resolves to ${ICON_PATH}/<icon>.png. Pick from Brad's theme inventory: os_*, tool_*, func_*. Distinct icons per entry give a glanceable menu — no two boot targets share the same glyph.

order.label: NixOS - Fresh Desktop
order._note: Full Plasma desktop with `noresume` + safe hibernate-image invalidation. The everyday 'ignore my saved session, start clean' choice — Primary auto-resumes a hibernate image when one exists; this entry never does. Added 2026-06-12.

order.label: BlissOS - Android
order._note: BlissOS x86_64 installed-to-folder on p5 (Shared-Lib, /blissos) — see ~/git/unix/ae_desk-android_x86_blissOS. rEFInd boots it DIRECTLY (native linux_partition stanza: volume=p5 UUID, loader=/blissos/kernel, initrd=/blissos/initrd.img, options from grub.menu.blissos with root_param=/dev/ram0). No GRUB chainload needed — /blissos/kernel is a real file (not a symlink like Debian/Kali's /vmlinuz), so rEFInd's ext4 driver loads it. No native partition (NVMe is full); reversible (delete /blissos + this entry).

order.label: my-konsole Rescue
order._note: Chainloads p8's /EFI/boot/bootx64.efi (grub.menu.mykonsole.efi_uuid = nvme0n1p8 UUID; ext4 via rEFInd's bundled ext4_x64 driver). p8 holds the my-konsole NixOS live-ISO tree relabelled MY_KONSOLE; its baked GRUB carries the volatile init= and finds nix-store.squashfs by label. No kernel/initrd/init here — nothing goes stale on ISO rebuild. Populate: ca_ventoy_fallback_usb/my-konsole/build.sh install-partition.

order.label: GRUB (fallback)
order._note: Chainloads /EFI/bootloader/grubx64.efi (the co-installed GRUB) as a fallback multiboot menu

order.label: Memory Test
order._note: memtest86+ 7.00 — full RAM diagnostic; runs without an OS. Lengthy (multiple passes); leave running for hours.

order.label: Network Boot
order._note: iPXE — open netboot. Drops to iPXE shell; useful for HTTP-chain into a rescue ISO or installer.

order.label: EFI Shell
order._note: EDK2 UEFI Shell — pre-OS firmware prompt. NOT a Linux shell (no curl/wget/nmtui); use NixOS - Rescue (native install) for those.

order.label: Reload rEFInd
order._label_note: ASCII-only labels — rEFInd's default PNG glyph atlas covers U+0020-U+007E. Em dashes render as '??'.

grub._description: GRUB install settings + UI + menu entries. Kept for fallback during Phase 4 rEFInd transition. Once rEFInd is verified, this block can be deleted.
grub._linux_order_note: Order in which non-NixOS Linux distros render in grub.cfg. Each entry MUST be a key in grub.menu.* with kernel/initrd/root_uuid set. The renderer's emit_linux_partition is fully generic — adding a distro is a 2-line edit (new grub.menu.<key> object + append to linux_order), no engine change.
grub._efi_chainload_order_note: EFI-binary chainload entries in grub.cfg (emit_efi_chainload) — for OSes whose own EFI bootloader carries a volatile/self-contained cmdline we don't want to reproduce (e.g. a NixOS live-ISO tree on a partition: its baked GRUB owns the /nix/store/<hash>/init path). Each key MUST be a grub.menu.<key> with efi_uuid + efi_path; renderer is fs-agnostic (insmod fat+ext2). rEFInd side is the parallel efi_chainload producer.

nixos._description: NixOS entries. Phase 1: NixOS auto-generates them. Phase 3: aa_bootloader walks /nix/var/nix/profiles/system-*-link.

debian.label: Debian Rescue OS
debian._efi_note: rEFInd chainloads the co-installed GRUB at /EFI/bootloader/grubx64.efi (owned by aa_bootloader). debian-installer never dropped a /EFI/debian/ on the ESP — confirmed 2026-05-07. Once GRUB takes over, its richer ext4 driver follows Debian's /vmlinuz and /initrd.img symlinks correctly, where rEFInd's ext4_x64.efi cannot. The kernel/initrd/options fields above are consumed by render-grub-cfg.sh to add this menuentry to the same GRUB binary that's chainloaded here — closing the loop.
debian._note: Replaces Arch on p6 (2026-05-03). Debian trixie minimal CLI rescue OS with Node + Claude Code + Firefox-for-OAuth. Kernel paths use Debian's auto-updating /vmlinuz and /initrd.img symlinks at the FS root — kernel upgrades via apt are picked up automatically. rEFInd reads p6 directly via ext4 driver (volume label = 'rescue-os-debian'); ESP is too small (100 MB) to host every distro's initrd.

blissos.label: BlissOS - Android
blissos._refind_volume_note: rEFInd's `volume` token matches a filesystem LABEL / partition label / partition GPT GUID (PARTUUID) — NOT the ext4 filesystem UUID (root_uuid). Using root_uuid here made rEFInd unable to resolve p5 → 'kernel not found' even with /blissos/kernel present. p5's fs label 'Shared-Lib' is stable (no relabel), matches how NixOS entries use volume "boot". root_uuid stays for GRUB search --fs-uuid / root=UUID=.
blissos._efi_note: Consumed by rEFInd's linux_partition producer (NOT GRUB — blissos is intentionally absent from grub.linux_order). rEFInd emits a native stanza: volume=root_uuid (p5), loader=kernel, initrd=initrd, options="root=<root_param> <options>". rEFInd's ext4_x64.efi driver reads /blissos/kernel directly because it is a real file (Debian/Kali need GRUB only because their /vmlinuz is a relative symlink rEFInd can't follow).
blissos._note: BlissOS x86_64 installed-to-folder on p5 (NVMe is fully partitioned — no native partition). The /blissos tree ({kernel,initrd.img,system.efs,data.img}) is laid down by ~/git/unix/ae_desk-android_x86_blissOS/install/build.sh from the pinned release in blissos.json. SRC=/blissos tells the initrd where system.efs lives; DATA= (empty) uses data.img inside SRC. root_param=/dev/ram0 (ramdisk root); root_uuid=p5 UUID (rEFInd volume + kernel/initrd file source). Reversible: delete /blissos + this menu entry + the refind manual_stanzas entry.

mykonsole.label: my-konsole Rescue
mykonsole._refind_volume_note: p8's PARTUUID (GPT partition GUID). rEFInd matches label/PARTUUID, not the ext4 fs UUID (efi_uuid). PARTUUID is used (not the label) because install-partition RELABELS p8 to MY_KONSOLE — a label would go stale, the PARTUUID survives. efi_uuid stays for GRUB's fs-agnostic search side.
mykonsole._note: my-konsole NixOS live-ISO tree extracted onto p8 (nvme0n1p8, ext4). Populated by ca_ventoy_fallback_usb/my-konsole/build.sh install-partition, which rsyncs the whole ISO fs to p8 and relabels it MY_KONSOLE (= isoImage.volumeID) so the ISO's baked GRUB finds nix-store.squashfs by label. Both rEFInd (efi_chainload producer) and GRUB (emit_efi_chainload) CHAINLOAD p8's own /EFI/boot/bootx64.efi — the volatile init=/nix/store/<hash>/init lives inside that GRUB, never in boot.json. efi_uuid is the stable partition UUID (survives the relabel). Reversible: wipe p8 + drop this key + the two order entries.

kali.label: Kali Linux
kali._efi_note: rEFInd chainloads the co-installed GRUB at /EFI/bootloader/grubx64.efi (owned by aa_bootloader). The Kali installer never dropped a /EFI/kali/ on the ESP — confirmed 2026-05-07. The previous 'Invalid Loader File!' came from the linux_partition producer pointing rEFInd's ext4_x64.efi at /vmlinuz, which it cannot follow as a relative symlink. Once GRUB takes over, its richer ext4 driver resolves the symlink. The kernel/initrd/options fields above are consumed by render-grub-cfg.sh to add this menuentry to the same GRUB binary that's chainloaded here.

grub_fallback._description: rEFInd-side shortcut that chainloads the co-installed GRUB EFI binary (efi_install_dir = /EFI/bootloader). Reachable from rEFInd via the efi_chainload producer. Purely a rEFInd convenience entry — not consumed by the GRUB renderer (would be circular).
grub_fallback.label: GRUB (fallback)

efi_shell._description: EDK2 UEFI Shell — minimal interactive prompt at firmware level. Vendored at src/loaders/refind/vendored/efi-tools/shellx64.efi (from nixpkgs.edk2-uefi-shell), staged to ESP at /EFI/refind/tools/shellx64.efi by render-refind-binary.sh. Use cases: low-level EFI debugging, NVRAM tweaks, fs traversal when nothing else boots. NOT a Linux shell — it's UEFI bytecode, no networking/wget/curl/nmtui.
efi_shell.label: EFI Shell

memtest._description: Memtest86+ — RAM tester. Boots via Linux EFI-stub. Vendored from nixpkgs.memtest86plus 7.00 → /EFI/refind/tools/memtest86.efi. Reachable as top-row entry (manual_stanzas) AND as bottom-row 'memtest' showtools button.
memtest.label: Memory Test

ipxe._description: iPXE — open network bootloader. Vendored from nixpkgs.ipxe → /EFI/refind/tools/ipxe.efi. Reachable as top-row 'Network Boot' entry AND as bottom-row 'netboot' showtools button. Drops to iPXE shell where you can dhcp + chain http/tftp/iSCSI/etc.
ipxe.label: Network Boot

kernel._description: Hibernate-related kernel cmdline. Other params (mem_sleep_default, splash, psi, audit, loglevel) come from configuration_power.nix and nixos-hardware in Phase 1. Phase 3 may consolidate.

rescue-current-gen._description: Rescue (current generation) strips hibernation cmdline so a fresh boot is forced. Same kernel/initrd/custom modules as the default boot — fast-path config-bug fallback. Phase 1: configuration_rescue.nix uses lib.mkForce; this JSON captures intent. Phase 3: kernel_params.nix consumes this. Renamed 2026-05-07 from 'rescue' to disambiguate from 'rescue-native-install'.

rescue-native-install._description: Rescue (native-install) — clean module set, NO custom watchdog/protection/observability/containers. Full dev environment (gcc, git, vim/neovim, tmux, ripgrep, btrfs/cryptsetup tools, node+npm for `npx claude-code`). All persistent btrfs subvolumes still mounted. Same hibernation-cmdline strip as rescue-current-gen so the boot is always fresh. Future Phase: route through a pinned nixpkgs flake input for full insulation against nixpkgs drift. Added 2026-05-07.

safe-graphics._description: GNOME-on-X11 fallback. configuration_fallback.nix owns the desktop overrides; this JSON only describes cmdline diff.

fresh-desktop._description: Fresh Desktop — full Plasma session that deliberately ignores any saved hibernate image (`noresume`) and safely invalidates it (swapfile-header rewrite via configuration_rescue_invalidate_hibernate.nix, never the partition — 2026-06-12 incident). The boot-menu counterpart to Primary's auto-resume: Primary = continue session from disk, Fresh Desktop = start clean. configuration_fresh_desktop.nix uses lib.mkForce; this JSON captures intent.

swap_hibernate._description: Swap + hibernation resume target. POST-INCIDENT (2026-05-15): moved OFF the btrfs pool. Root cause of the 2026-05-15 pool destruction was a btrfs swapfile whose CoW-relocatable extents overlapped live metadata chunks — the hibernate write went to the swapfile's current extent locations (legal), which had drifted onto chunk 73's metadata mirrors at physical 39.1/39.5 GB, bytewise clobbering them (DUP mirrors with divergent bytes — impossible for btrfs to produce, conclusive). The new design eliminates the failure mode at the root: swapfile lives on the ext4 Shared-Lib partition (p5, fixed extents, no CoW), AND the resume target is independent of the pool device. Pool failure cannot break hibernate; hibernate cannot break the pool.
swap_hibernate.isolation_invariant: resume_device MUST NOT be on the same physical device or filesystem as any subvol that holds live OS state. The ext4 partition holding the swapfile MUST be mounted on every NixOS boot before sleep.target. Enforced by swap_hibernate.nix (nix assertion), configuration_pre-hibernate-warning.nix (preflight ExecStartPre), and configuration_swapfile_resume_check.nix (hard refuse on drift).
swap_hibernate._resume_offset_note: Populated by `aa_bootloader/build.sh deploy --target nixos` at deploy time via `filefrag -v -b4096 <swapfile>` after mkswap. ext4 swapfiles have FIXED extents — this value is stable until the swapfile is explicitly recreated. No self-healer for the WRITE side; the check service now ENFORCES the invariant and refuses to hibernate on drift.
swap_hibernate._kernel_params_note: Empty until deploy populates resume_offset. The renderer in build.sh substitutes @RESUME_OFFSET@ at deploy. swap_hibernate.nix asserts at build time that kernel_params is non-empty if the swap is configured to be present.

hibernate_invalidation._description: Any boot path that mounts the pool from a context that might modify it MUST first invalidate any pending hibernate image on the swap device. The kernel only resumes if a valid `S1SUSPEND` signature sits at the swap header — overwrite that signature with `SWAPSPACE2` (clean swap) and the kernel falls through to cold boot. Idempotent and cheap (one 4-KiB write or one mkswap call).
hibernate_invalidation._method_note: The resume target is a SWAPFILE inside the ext4 Shared-Lib filesystem — the swap header (and any S1SUSPEND hibernate signature) lives in the FIRST PAGE OF THE FILE, not of the partition. Invalidation = mkswap on the FILE PATH, through the mounted filesystem. ext4 extents are fixed, so this rewrites the header in place without moving the file — resume_offset stays valid. NEVER run mkswap/dd against the partition or /dev/disk/by-label/Shared-Lib: that device IS the ext4 filesystem; writing its first 4 KiB destroys the primary superblock (2026-06-12 incident — the previous declared method did exactly this, killed the fslabel, made /mnt/shared-lib unmountable, left only zram swap, and the battery watchdog's hibernate calls failed with 'Not enough suitable swap space' until the machine drained dead; recovered via fsck.ext4 -b 32768).
hibernate_invalidation._scope_note: Runs ONLY in the rescue specialisations listed in trigger_specialisations (their cmdline carries `noresume`), guarded by ConditionKernelCommandLine=noresume as defense-in-depth. It must NEVER run on a normal boot — a normal boot resumes via resume=/resume_offset= and the kernel itself consumes the signature.

_pool_witness._description: Detects out-of-band pool mounts. configuration_pool_witness.nix writes a fresh nonce to @shared/.pool-witness/id on every clean mount in NixOS, mirrors it to /run/pool-witness/current-mount.id, and persists the last clean value at /var/lib/pool-witness/last-clean-mount.id. If the on-disk nonce at next NixOS mount differs from the recorded last-clean value, something else touched the pool — preflight refuses to hibernate so we don't write an image whose RAM-state-of-the-pool will be inconsistent with the disk.
